concept.concept_description: The natural extension of the triangle map (a multi-dimensional continued fraction algorithm) admits a Z/2Z symmetry action generated by an involution τ corresponding to Young conjugation of integer partitions. This involution preserves the invariant measure on the natural extension space and permutes four distinguished subdomains D₁, D₂, D₃, D₄ into each other. Specifically, τ maps each subdomain to another in a 4-cycle or involution pattern, and each subdomain carries exactly 1/4 of the total measure. This symmetry generalizes the classical case for the Gauss map and Farey map, where Young conjugation provides a new perspective on previously known symmetries.
concept.mathematical_framing: The natural extension of the triangle map (a multi-dimensional continued fraction algorithm) admits a Z/2Z symmetry action generated by an involution τ corresponding to Young conjugation of integer partitions. This involution preserves the invariant measure on the natural extension space and permutes four distinguished subdomains D₁, D₂, D₃, D₄ into each other. Specifically, τ maps each subdomain to another in a 4-cycle or involution pattern, and each subdomain carries exactly 1/4 of the total measure. This symmetry generalizes the classical case for the Gauss map and Farey map, where Young conjugation provides a new perspective on previously known symmetries.
concept.lean_guess: 1) Construct the natural extension of the triangle map as a measure-preserving dynamical system in dimension n. 2) Define the Young conjugation involution τ on integer partitions and lift it to the natural extension space via the partition-triangle map correspondence. 3) Prove τ is measure-preserving and an involution (τ² = id). 4) Identify the four subdomains explicitly in terms of the triangle map coordinates and show τ permutes them. 5) Verify the measure of each subdomain equals 1/4 of the total space. The proof will use the symplectic dot product structure [k̄] · (λ̄)ᵀ = N to establish the conjugation symmetry.
